title: Input-conditioned Mirror modulation network
hypothesis: A low-description context-to-Mirror-code generator reproduces held-out sample-conditioned functions with better payload/compute than FiLM, generic dynamic filters, and direct coefficient generation.
physical_object: shared 8x8 operator and fixed orthogonal rotation basis
logical_multiplicity: sample-specific functions over continuous two-dimensional context

development.selection_metric: heldout output nMSE, actual serialized bytes, generator and operator MAC proxy

fresh.reason: Direct two-basis coefficient control is evaluated before fresh split.

storage.authority: actual deterministic NPZ inference payload bytes

success_gate: Mirror output nMSE <=1e-4, >=10% fewer bytes than FiLM and generic dynamic filter, and >=10% smaller than direct coefficient generator at matched quality.
failure_gate: Direct coefficient control matches Mirror within 1% bytes/quality or output quality fails.
boundaries: no natural input or Transformer claim
fresh remains sealed if specificity gate fails
Direct two-basis coefficient representation was charged only for shared W and context map; fixed J is deterministic, making its serialized state identical to Mirror.
